## Answer Key: Chapter 6 {#sec-solutions-ch6}

Full solutions to Chapter 6's "Check your understanding" questions
(@sec-ch6).

**1. Quick check.** *Answer.* Group size $=H_q/H_{kv}=128/8=16$. Since
$1 < H_{kv} < H_q$, this is GQA, not MHA ($H_{kv}=H_q$) or MQA
($H_{kv}=1$).

**2. Quick check.** *Answer.* Only the routed expert bank's ratio --
attention, the shared expert, and every other always-active component
also count toward the whole model's active fraction, which stays
closer to 1 than the bank-level $k/E$ ratio (ch. 5).

**3. Compare.** *Answer.* Llama 3's growing state is present in every
one of its 126 layers (all attention). Jamba's growing state exists
only in its 4 attention layers out of 32 -- the other 28 keep a
fixed-size recurrent state instead.

**4. Misconception check.** *Answer.* False. Measured model quality
depends on architecture together with training data, training recipe,
optimization, evaluation methodology, and serving implementation --
none of the three case studies' architectural choices alone determines
how well, how cheaply, or how reliably the resulting model performs.
*Common trap:* treating one architectural feature (more experts, a
newer mechanism) as a stand-in for overall quality.

**5. Design exercise (applied exercise).** *Answer.* (a) Group size
$=32/8=4$. (b) Attention layers' KV-cache grows with context; recurrent
layers' state stays fixed size. (c) 2 of 64 routed experts active per
token plus 1 shared; all 64 still stored. (d) All-to-all dispatch if
the 64 experts are device-split (ch. 5). (e) GQA (ch. 3), local/global
attention (ch. 4), routed MoE with a shared expert (ch. 5), and a
recurrent/state-space layer (ch. 6) are all present. (f) Quality,
latency, training recipe, and serving cost cannot be read off the
config alone. *Interview criteria:* separates the bank ratio from any
whole-model claim; names a non-inferable conclusion.

**6. Interview practice.** *Answer.* Head counts/cache representation
predict memory; dense-vs-MoE and active parameters predict compute;
whether experts/layers are device-split predicts communication --
latency, throughput, and quality are explicitly not predicted from
architecture alone. *Interview criteria:* covers memory, compute,
*and* communication; refuses to overclaim benchmark performance.
